subject: Pilot SLA flexibility and proposed remedial credits
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah@helixware.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Purchasing <purchasing@helixware.com>, Infra Team <infra@helixware.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot SLA request: temporary uptime adjustment

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — team is excited to get the pilot live. We ran the traffic simulations this morning and a couple of constraints popped up on our side (bursty telemetry ingestion across a small set of regional clients).

Ask: for the 30-day pilot, would Redwood consider a temporary adjustment to the uptime target from 99.95% to 99.80% with a capped remedial credit instead of the standard service-credit ladder? Our procurement team wants a single, predictable makeup credit and an extended support window while we stabilize.

We can accept a one-time onboarding credit and agree to a weekly operational sync. Attached a short pilot traffic PDF and our security questionnaire.

Attachments: pilot_traffic_report.pdf, Helixware_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

Appreciate a quick answer — the pilot start is targeted for next Monday.

Best,
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform
Helixware Inc.

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah@helixware.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA request: temporary uptime adjustment

Team — looping you in. Helixware is asking for a temporary SLO waiver (99.95 -> 99.80) for the pilot window and prefers a single capped makeup credit plus a one-time onboarding credit and extended support hours. They will run heavy bursts from a small region which we expect to mitigate with routing/fallbacks but could still impact availability early on.

Proposed internal commercial terms (what I plan to escalate for exec signoff):
- Pilot length: 30 days (start next Monday)
- Temporary uptime target: 99.80% (pilot window only)
- Remedy: single capped makeup credit = up to 5% of monthly pilot invoice (flat cap) for any uptime shortfall during pilot period
- Additional concession: one-time onboarding credit equal to one week of billed usage (applied as invoice credit)
- Operational guardrails: mandatory weekly ops sync, read-only access for Helixware to troubleshooting traces for the pilot, and a mutually agreed fallback plan to a lower-throughput model variant if severe instability observed

Risks/notes:
- This reduces our exposure to an open-ended credit ladder but loosens the SLO.
- Legal needs to confirm language for the temporary amendment + rollback clause at pilot end.
- Finance — need quick estimate of revenue impact for the credit cap.

Can I get a point approval to take to Marcus for an exec signoff? If we get Marcus' OK we can commit to Helixware tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah@helixware.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA request: temporary uptime adjustment

Logan — I support moving quickly here. A few edits to your proposed terms:

1) Change remedy cap to tiered credit: 2.5% for first week of shortfall, 5% max cumulative for entire pilot. Keeps predictable exposure while giving Helixware runway.
2) Require a formal rollback clause: SLO returns to 99.95% at pilot close or earlier if Helixware requests production promotion.
3) Add requirement: Helixware must provide their traffic simulator seed and a post-pilot health report; otherwise credit triggers default.

I've summarized this as a short one-page exhibit (attached). Legal picks up the temporary amendment language; Finance please run a quick model of max cost if we hit the full 5%.

Attachment: proposed_remedy_summary.xlsx

-Marissa
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah@helixware.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA request: temporary uptime adjustment

Quick note — I prefer Marissa's tiered cap approach. Commercially, Helixware is very promising and a short concession to get the pilot live makes sense, but can we push for a 10% pilot discount (first 30 days) instead of or stacked with the onboarding credit? That keeps cash in play and simplifies accounting.

If Marcus signs off on the tiered cap + 10% first-month discount, I will approve the go-ahead.

-Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah@helixware.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Pilot SLA request: temporary uptime adjustment — EXEC APPROVAL

Approved with conditions.

Decision summary:
- Approved temporary SLO for pilot: 99.80% for a 30-day window starting on agreed kickoff date.
- Remedy: tiered makeup credit as Marissa proposed (2.5% first-week shortfall, up to 5% cumulative cap for pilot).
- Additional concessions: 10% pilot discount (Ben's recommendation) + one-time onboarding credit (applied if Helixware completes required simulator handoff).
- Operational requirements: weekly ops sync (internal + Helixware), designated on-call engineer from Redwood during the pilot window (Pacific hours overlap), and a rollback clause that restores 99.95% SLO at pilot close.

Conditions before commitment to Helixware:
1) Legal to draft a 1-page temporary amendment with explicit start/end dates and the rollback clause.
2) Finance to confirm the maximum exposure (credits + discount) and confirm accounting treatment.
3) Helixware must provide the traffic simulator seed and sign the amendment.

Logan — take this to Legal and Finance. If both sign off, you have my exec authorization to finalize and send the amendment to Helixware. Thanks for moving fast on this — high priority given potential expansion.

Marcus Lin
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
